questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Healthy food and habits vocabulary
questions.prompt: Which of these is a dairy food?
questions.evidence: Dairy foods come from milk. Cheese, milk and yoghurt are dairy; rice and lettuce belong to other food groups.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The four food groups
questions.prompt: Which food group gives you energy to work and play?
questions.evidence: The lesson text says that meat and fish give you energy to work and play.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The four food groups
questions.prompt: Bread, rice and cereal belong to which food group?
questions.evidence: The text names wheat, cereal and rice as grains, and says grains should be in every meal.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Advice with should and shouldn’t
questions.prompt: You _____ spend a long time playing computer games.
questions.evidence: The Let’s Learn box says: You shouldn’t spend a long time playing computer games.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Suggestions with Why don’t you …?
questions.evidence: A suggestion that is a question begins Why don’t you …? “You should” and “You shouldn’t” cannot form a question.

questions.prompt: Omar is always tired at school. Choose the best advice.
questions.evidence: Going to bed earlier helps a tired pupil. “You shouldn’t get enough sleep” advises the opposite, and “Why don’t you sleep late?” suggests a later bedtime.
options: a) You shouldn’t get enough sleep.
b) Why don’t you sleep late?
c) You should go to bed earlier.

questions.evidence: “You should …” is the advice form taught in the lesson. The others are a statement about the speaker and a question.
options: a) I drink lots of water.
b) You should drink lots of water.
c) Do you drink lots of water?

questions.evidence: Milk, bread and an apple come from the dairy, grains and fruit groups. Sweets and cola are unhealthy, and coffee alone is not a healthy breakfast.
options: c) milk, bread and an apple

questions.prompt: Choose True or False: You should drink lots of water every day.
questions.evidence: The advice in the lesson says that everyone should drink lots of water every day.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: The four food groups
questions.prompt: Choose True or False: Fruit and vegetables are full of vitamins.
questions.evidence: The “My Plate” text says fruit and vegetables are full of vitamins.

questions.prompt: Choose True or False: Eating many sweets is good for your teeth.
questions.evidence: The lesson says eating too many sweets is bad for you, and dairy is the food group that makes teeth strong.
Everyone takes should, not shouldn’t, and “why don’t you” cannot follow everyone in a statement.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about healthy habits
questions.prompt: Read the text. What does Rami eat for breakfast?
questions.evidence: The third sentence lists bread, cheese and an apple for breakfast.
options: a) bread, cheese and an apple

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about healthy habits
questions.prompt: In the text, how does Rami go to school?
questions.evidence: The text says Rami walks to school with his sister, so he goes on foot.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about healthy habits
questions.prompt: In the text, what does Rami do after school?
questions.evidence: The text says that after school Rami plays football in the park.
options: b) he watches television for a long time

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Reading a short text about healthy habits
questions.prompt: In the text, choose True or False: Rami goes to bed late.
questions.evidence: The text says Rami goes to bed at nine o’clock, so he does not go to bed late.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing advice with should
questions.prompt: Make one complete sentence of advice with these words: you / should / get / enough / sleep
questions.evidence: Should is followed by the plain verb: you should get enough sleep.

questions.objectiveLabel: Lesson objective: Writing a suggestion with Why don’t you …?
questions.prompt: Make one question with these words: why / don’t / you / walk / every / day
questions.correct: Why don’t you walk every day?
accepted: why don’t you walk every day
questions.wrongSample: Why don’t you walking every day?
questions.evidence: Why don’t you is followed by the plain verb and the question ends with a question mark.
